how_scored.pick_rule: Best average score across 5 climate views x 2 price scenarios under the farmer's priorities
how_scored.profit_basis: Return above variable costs (land and machinery cost the same whichever rotation is planted); cost-share shown separately, not scored

economics.winter_wheat: Texas A&M AgriLife 2024 District 8 HRW wheat budget (48 bu); Ellis Co. NASS 2021-23 avg 48 bu
economics.corn: AgriLife 2024 District 8 reduced-till corn budget; yield = Ellis Co. NASS 2021-23 avg (71, 60, 92)
economics.sorghum: AgriLife 2024 District 8 grain sorghum budget (45 cwt = 80 bu). Ellis Co. NASS shows one undated year at 48 bu, likely a dry year
economics.soybean_dc: AgriLife 2025 District 11 dryland soybean budget (30 bu, $6.89/bu variable); ASSUMPTION: 25 bu double-crop yield, $15 fixed

sources.prices: USDA WASDE / ERS: 2025/26 final or latest (wheat $5.06, corn $4.15, sorghum $3.55, soybean $10.20); 2026/27 forecasts (wheat $6.20, corn $4.60, sorghum $4.30, soybean $11.40)
sources.eqip: EQIP rates listed by the Texas Climate Smart Initiative (tcsi.tamu.edu); confirm with the Ellis County NRCS office
sources.nitrogen: Texas A&M AgriLife N rates (1.5 lb/bu wheat, ~1 lb/bu corn under 100 bu, 2 lb/100 lb sorghum); urea $0.72/lb N (DTN, Nov 2026)

pests.wheat_leaf_rust: Leaf rust: infection best at 59-77 F with rain or heavy dew (Texas A&M AgriLife). Index = spring days in that range with moisture.
pests.wheat_continuity: Wheat every year keeps residue-borne diseases and pests (Hessian fly, tan spot) and the summer 'green bridge' for wheat curl mite and wheat streak mosaic going. A non-host summer crop or prompt volunteer control breaks it.
pests.sugarcane_aphid: Sugarcane aphid: thrives in warm, dry weather; mild winters let it overwinter as far north as Central Texas; very high summer heat suppresses it.
pests.aflatoxin: Aflatoxin in corn: drought and heat (especially hot nights) around silking and grain fill.
pests.charcoal_rot: Charcoal rot in soybean: hot, dry weather during flowering and pod fill.
pests.cotton_root_rot: Not in these rotations. If cotton is added: Blackland soils favor cotton root rot; rotating with grass crops (wheat, corn, sorghum) reduces it.

assumptions: Double-crop soybean yield 25 bu and $15 fixed cost
Half of legume cover N available to next crop
Year types from Model 3 (k-means on 1985-2025 NASA POWER seasons; soft groups, 41 years)
